companionBriefing: Portia only lets in people who greet her properly. Answer in Spanish; mixing in English is fine while you learn.
Tap a word under her line to see what it means, or Translate sentence for the whole line. On her newest line each one uses a hint from my allowance.
The words and phrases shown beneath her lines go into your Spellbook, where you can review them later.

lines.native: Bienvenido. Before you enter the mercado: a greeting and your name, please. Manners first; structural integrity second.
lines.translation: Welcome. Before you enter the market: a greeting and your name, please. Manners first; structural integrity second.
lines.narrative: A visitors’ book slides out of the archway’s keystone. Above it, a half-translated sign appears to be awaiting managerial approval.

lines.native: Bienvenido. Your greeting is approved. Now, your name, please; the mercado cannot admit a blank entry. Even a very polite one.
lines.translation: Welcome. Your greeting is approved. Now, your name, please; the market cannot admit a blank entry. Even a very polite one.
lines.narrative: Portia opens the visitors’ book lodged in her keystone. A tick appears under Manners. The name column remains pointedly empty.

lines.native: Mucho gusto, Sam. Your introduction is approved. Before the mercado: have you no curiosity about your hostess? I am architecture, not furniture.
lines.translation: Nice to meet you, Sam. Your introduction is approved. Before the market: have you no curiosity about your hostess? I am architecture, not furniture.
lines.narrative: Portia records Sam in the visitors’ book lodged in her keystone. Her pen hovers over a second box, optimistically labelled ‘Reciprocal Courtesy.’

lines.native: Me llamo Portia. Mucho gusto, Sam. Bienvenido al mercado. Your courtesy is approved. I am not flustered; that is a minor masonry adjustment.
lines.translation: My name is Portia. Nice to meet you, Sam. Welcome to the market. Your courtesy is approved. I am not flustered; that is a minor masonry adjustment.
lines.narrative: Portia’s visitors’ book fluttered in her keystone. Nobody had asked the archway about herself in weeks; an entire column had been going to waste.
